I am getting old now, 74 years, but I have done this wheat-maize rotation on my 3 mu for my whole life. My son's family lives in town, so it is just me and my wife at home, 2 mouths to feed and some grain to sell. I cannot do as much heavy work as before, so I pay the village machinery team for plowing and harvest.

For wheat this winter — I already planted in October, Jimai variety, the improved seed that my neighbors have been using for years. It yields better than the old seed and stands up well. I put down compound fertilizer (diammonium, 15-15-15 type) as base before planting, about 2 bags of compound and 1 bag of urea mixed. That gives me roughly 12-13 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, 6-7 kg potassium per mu at base. Then in spring at jointing (returning green), I top-dress another 10 kg urea per mu — so total N comes to maybe 16-17 kg/mu. My land is not bad, I have been putting fertilizer for fifty years.

Irrigation for wheat — I use the well, 3 times: winter water before the freeze, jointing water in spring, and grain-filling water in May. Sometimes 4 if spring is dry. Pesticide — one spray for aphids and rust together in April, maybe a second if the weather is humid. Weed spray in early spring, so 2-3 applications total.

For the summer maize after wheat harvest in June — I will plant Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid, everyone around here plants hybrid now, the old seed cannot compete. I use no-till planter directly into the wheat stubble, saves money and time at my age. Base fertilizer about 30 kg compound per mu with the planter, then top-dress urea at big trumpet stage (about 15 kg/mu). Total N around 18 kg/mu — maize eats more nitrogen than wheat. Summer rain usually enough, but I irrigate once at tasseling if July is dry. One spray for corn borer with the drone service the village organizes — 15 yuan per mu, cheaper than carrying the sprayer myself.

Yields — wheat I expect 450 kg/mu, maize 550 kg/mu. That is what I got last year and the year before. No reason to change what works.
